title: REGAL reinforcement learning designs tissue-specific enhancers across species
summary: REGAL uses reinforcement learning to program enhancer regulatory grammar under sequence-to-function oracles. Designed enhancers drove predicted lineage-specific expression in transgenic mouse embryos, outperformed a nucleotide-level optimizer in human cells, and matched or exceeded leading designs in zebrafish and Drosophila at shorter length. Perturbations showed tissue specificity needs both target activation and off-target repression. Only the abstract was reviewed, so numbers are not available.
ai_technology: REGAL reinforcement learning over transcription factor motif placement with sequence-to-function oracles

evidence.tested: Reporter experiments in transgenic mouse embryos, human cells, zebrafish and Drosophila, plus motif perturbations.
evidence.unknown: Quantitative success rates; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement learning generated the enhancer designs that were tested.
